**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mask SSH private keys and passphrases in import request logs**

When `import_file()` receives `ssh_tunnel_private_keys` or `ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords`, it places their JSON-encoded values in `data`, but neither key is recognized by this sensitive-key set. Consequently, `RequestHandler.request_with_retry()` logs the complete private keys and passphrases at DEBUG through `mask_request_kwargs()`. Add both import fields to the masking rules so enabling request diagnostics does not expose database SSH credentials.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebuild the query context before validating its stale contents**

After loading a chart with a stored query context, changing an existing params value such as `row_limit` and calling `derive_query_context()` still makes serialization fail: `super().to_json()` runs `_check_tree()` and `Chart.validate()` against the old `query_context.form_data` before the replacement occurs. Likewise, a new chart supplied with populated options can fail validation on its empty intermediate query list. Derive the replacement before validating the context that will actually be sent; otherwise the documented params-to-query-context workflow cannot save these charts.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Extract the Y-axis column before resolving its label**

For a heatmap with `normalize_across="y"`, `groupby` is a one-element list, as required by `HeatmapOption.validate()` and produced by `add_simple_dimension()`. Passing that list to `column_label()` raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`, so generating or saving the chart fails instead of producing its query context. Resolve the label of the selected Y-axis column rather than the list containing it.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the table datasource default for newly built charts**

Creating a chart with only `slice_name` and `datasource_id` previously defaulted `datasource_type` to `DatasourceType.TABLE`; it now silently defaults to `None`. `_fill_datasource()` interpolates that value into params as, for example, `"7__None"`, while serialization omits the required top-level `datasource_type` from the POST payload. Existing constructor usage therefore produces a chart that cannot be created in Superset. Restore the table default for newly constructed charts while retaining absent-field preservation when reading API objects.

causal_evidence: Commit 63726127687ebdd09e93398402224c1d8241c642 adds both SSH private-key import arguments and places their JSON-encoded values in data in supersetapiplus/base/base.py.
The masking implementation at that commit omits both field names from SENSITIVE_KEYS. Git confirms the supplied PR base is an ancestor of this commit.
The current worktree preserves the vulnerable import and logging path.
evidences: supersetapiplus/resources/repository.py:444-461 serializes ssh_tunnel_private_keys and ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords into data and passes it to client.post().
supersetapiplus/client.py:198-199 and :152-164 forward data to RequestHandler.request_with_retry().
supersetapiplus/transport/http.py:130 logs mask_request_kwargs(kwargs) at DEBUG.
supersetapiplus/core/masking.py:12-15 omits both names; :30-37 preserves their JSON strings, and :62-71 masks files separately.

A read-only reproduction using the worktree's mask_request_kwargs with synthetic import data reports secret_visible=True and field_masked=False for both affected fields. The ssh_tunnel_passwords control is masked.
payload.headline: SSH import private keys and passphrases leak into DEBUG logs
payload.before: Both SSH private-key import fields survive masking and appear in request diagnostics.
payload.after: Mask both fields before logging and add a regression test covering their JSON-encoded import values.
payload.motivation: Enabling DEBUG logging exposes SSH credentials supplied during imports.
payload.reply: Confirmed with synthetic import data: both fields survive mask_request_kwargs(), whose result is logged at DEBUG. Add both names to SENSITIVE_KEYS and regression coverage. The vulnerable path was introduced by 63726127687ebdd09e93398402224c1d8241c642.

causal_evidence: git show 57af98dc33d7e9591815b2e29d18ab3d00511607 -- supersetapiplus/charts/charts.py mostra a introdução de derive_query_context() e da substituição do contexto depois de super().to_json(columns).
Nesse commit, supersetapiplus/base/base.py:670-671 já executava self.validate() durante to_dict(convert_to_json=True), antes da substituição.
git merge-base confirma que o commit causal está entre a base 979ee37193ded3360a06b2751f4217e1a17236df e o head 0b966f42d52960d82233f2aa50cc378f9ba2ab3f.
evidences: supersetapiplus/charts/charts.py:313-320: derive_query_context() apenas ativa uma flag.
supersetapiplus/charts/charts.py:326-330: super().to_json() precede a geração do contexto substituto.
supersetapiplus/core/api_model.py:127-140 e 165-172: a serialização executa _check_tree(), validando modelos aninhados e depois o próprio chart.
supersetapiplus/charts/charts.py:145-178: Chart.validate() rejeita valores divergentes entre params e query_context.form_data, inclusive em charts lidos do servidor.
supersetapiplus/charts/query_context.py:45: QueryContext.validate() rejeita queries vazio; Chart.instance() preenche form_data com as opções fornecidas sem gerar queries.
tests/unit/test_build_query.py:228-241 testa a derivação de um chart carregado sem modificar params, deixando o cenário alegado descoberto.
A reprodução dinâmica não executou: a importação do pacote falhou por ausência de shortuuid no ambiente disponível. A confirmação decorre do fluxo verificável no código.
payload.follow_up: Corrigir a ordem localmente em Chart e acrescentar regressões para alteração de row_limit em chart carregado e criação com opções preenchidas.
payload.headline: A validação do contexto antigo impede sua própria regeneração
payload.before: A serialização valida o contexto armazenado ou intermediário antes de calcular seu substituto.
payload.after: Quando a derivação estiver habilitada, gerar e validar o contexto que será enviado antes de serializar o payload.
payload.motivation: Permitir o fluxo documentado de alterar params e regenerar query_context, preservando a validação do resultado.
payload.reply: Achado confirmado pelo fluxo do código. derive_query_context() apenas ativa uma flag; super().to_json() valida primeiro o contexto antigo e pode lançar uma exceção antes da derivação. É necessária uma correção local em Chart e cobertura dos dois cenários citados.
payload.ca_dod_impact: O fluxo documentado de regeneração após editar params fica impedido, assim como a serialização de charts novos com opções válidas e contexto intermediário vazio.

causal_evidence: git blame attributes build_heatmap(), including the defective call at supersetapiplus/charts/build_query.py:903, to 14148a098d48670ffa678d8b83e1d35b58fc514c.
Comparing that commit with its parent confirms that it introduced both build_heatmap() and the heatmap_v2 dispatch entry.
evidences: supersetapiplus/charts/heatmap_v2.py:72 requires groupby to be a list containing exactly one Y-axis column.
supersetapiplus/charts/build_query.py:903 passes the entire groupby list to column_label(); line 88 calls .get() on every non-string argument.

Executing query_context_for() from the worktree with viz_type='heatmap_v2', x_axis='day', metric='count', groupby=['campus'] and normalize_across='y' reproduces AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'. A one-element list containing an adhoc column reproduces the same failure.
supersetapiplus/charts/charts.py:324 invokes query_context_for() for ui_query_context(); line 330 invokes it during serialization when query-context derivation is enabled.
tests/unit/test_build_query.py:168 supplies groupby='campus' as a scalar, bypassing the list shape required by HeatmapOption.validate().
payload.follow_up: Add regression coverage using one-element groupby lists for both physical and adhoc Y-axis columns.
payload.headline: Y-axis normalization crashes for valid heatmap dimensions
payload.before: The Y-normalization branch resolves the label of the entire groupby list and raises AttributeError.
payload.after: Resolve the label of the selected Y-axis column so query-context generation succeeds.
payload.motivation: A supported normalization setting prevents valid heatmaps from generating their query context and being serialized for saving.
payload.reply: Confirmed in the worktree: normalize_across='y' with groupby=['campus'] raises AttributeError at column_label(). HeatmapOption requires this one-element list shape, while the existing test uses a scalar. The branch needs to extract the selected Y-axis column before resolving its label, with regression coverage for physical and adhoc columns.

causal_evidence: Na base 979ee37193ded3360a06b2751f4217e1a17236df, Chart.datasource_type usa default_factory=lambda: DatasourceType.TABLE.
O diff de 46997e8109211ea7c7f5653c4932a4c92c7c35c2, presente no intervalo base..HEAD, substitui esse default por SerializableOptional[DatasourceType] = field(default=None).
O pai de 061c6d8541954dc95b3caf454b0adabb6ebeb49b já contém o default None: a migração para pydantic preservou o defeito.
payload.reviewer_claimed_origin: Regressão no PR: retirada do default DatasourceType.TABLE para charts construídos diretamente.
evidences: supersetapiplus/charts/charts.py:87 declara datasource_type = None; _fill_datasource(), na linha 140, interpola esse valor em params.datasource.

Reprodução na worktree: TableChart(slice_name='Synthetic chart', datasource_id=7), seguido de add_simple_metric(MetricType.COUNT) e to_json(columns=list(chart.POST_FIELDS)), produz params.datasource='7__None', omite datasource_type e gera query_context.datasource={'id': 7, 'type': 'None'}.
supersetapiplus/resources/repository.py:354-358 utiliza esse payload no POST.
tests/fixtures/superset_openapi_6.1.0.json:679-682 declara datasource_type obrigatório em ChartRestApi.post.
supersetapiplus/core/api_model.py:109-114 preserva campos ausentes na leitura como MissingField, permitindo distinguir esse comportamento do default de construção.
payload.headline: Chart construído sem datasource_type perde o default TABLE
payload.before: O construtor assume None, gera datasource inválido e omite um campo obrigatório do POST.
payload.after: Restaurar DatasourceType.TABLE como default de construção, preservando campos ausentes nos objetos lidos da API.
payload.motivation: Manter compatibilidade do construtor e gerar um payload válido para criação de charts.
payload.reply: Confirmado na worktree: o construtor sem datasource_type gera '7__None', e o payload omite datasource_type, obrigatório no schema de POST. A retirada do default ocorreu em 46997e8109211ea7c7f5653c4932a4c92c7c35c2, antes da migração para pydantic. É necessária correção com teste de regressão, preservando a ausência de campos na leitura.
payload.ca_dod_impact: Viola a compatibilidade do construtor e o contrato de conformidade dos payloads com o OpenAPI.
